Description En: Nestled within the Olsztyn Old Town, you climb a few stairs from the high street to reach this modern brasserie decked out in light neutral colours. There’s a traditional heart to the generous, rustic yet carefully executed dishes. Dishes like pork cheeks with mashed potatoes, beetroot and cider-braised cabbage have clean, distinct flavours courtesy of quality ingredients, judicious seasoning and well-timed cooking. Look out for the pistachio fondant to finish.

Name: Restauracja w Zatoce
Address: Boutique Hotel Amax, aleja Spacerowa 7, Mikołajki, 11-730, Poland
Description En: Set within the Boutique Hotel Amax at the heart of the picturesque Masurian Lake District, this slightly Baroque-looking restaurant sits on the shores of Lake Mikołajskie. Grab a table by the window or on the terrace to make the most of the views. The chefs proudly use the local larder in their full-flavoured dishes, including fish from the lake itself, while their own smokehouse is used for the likes of standout smoked eel with red cabbage smurkul.

Name: Kraft Bistro
Description En: Tucked away down a cul-de-sac filled with several other eateries, this understandably popular brasserie is underpinned by the flame-centric cooking of the Josper grill. Top-quality produce from jumbo prawns to beef tenderloin are grilled with skill and served with simple, complementary garnishes. Enjoy the cooking on the terrace, in the conservatory or in the main dining room near the buzzing open kitchen. The efficient team run the busy space with skill.

Name: Śląska Prohibicja
Description En: In the history-rich neighbourhood of Nikiszowiec, this large restaurant sits on the ground floor of what was once accommodation for local miners. In fact, you can still get a sense of the vintage canteen the dining room once was. Today, it’s enlivened by bookshelves and foliage, while the cooking offers hearty renditions of Polish and Silesian classics. A prime example is the breaded bone-in pork chop with piquant dried capers, cucumber salad and sour cream.

Name: Młodnik
Description En: A friendly welcome awaits at this family-run brasserie in the city suburbs. The interiors are decked out with modern furnishings and plenty of foliage, while a lovely paved terrace is the place to be when the sun is shining. The cooking offers clean, distinct flavours across dishes such as local herring with sour cream, apple and horseradish, as well as those with more of a Mediterranean influence. A strong version of the classic kogel mogel is a great way to finish.

Name: Restauracja Solmarina
Address: Grano Hotel Solmarina, Łąkowa 239, Wiślinka, 83-011, Poland
Description En: Located within the Grano Hotel Solmarina, this restaurant benefits from a striking location in a private marina with plenty of space for luxury boats and yachts. Inside, it's as stylish as you’d expect, with light flooding through the floor-to-ceiling windows. The cooking is rooted in Polish classics given a modern spin, like the delicious sour cucumber soup, served here with confit potato and a golden croquette of pulled pork rib.

Name: Mercado Tapas Bistro
Description En: This tapas bar under a red-brick railway arch brings a little slice of Spain to Lower Silesia. It’s got all the ingredients of a good night out, from the buzz of happy diners to a drinks list including Spanish wines, sherry and sangria. The cooking marries tapas staples, like croquetas and pan con tomate, with a ‘Something Different’ section incorporating well-judged international tweaks. The Basque cheesecake will provide a fitting finale to a terrific all-round experience.

Name: mayo
Description En: Tucked away in the city centre, this friendly little bistro offers a lovely atmosphere courtesy of its combination of on-view kitchen, exposed brick walls and slightly retro-style furniture – the polite, efficient team play their part too. The unpretentious, flavour-focused cooking has its roots in tradition but isn’t afraid of introducing a playful edge, exemplified by the rightly popular duck confit ‘doughnuts’ served with an excellent demi-glace sauce.

Name: Amfora
Description En: There’s a stylishly stripped-back look to this passionately run restaurant where the moody colour scheme and lighting set the scene for a globetrotting meal. The menu is inspired by the chef’s travels and features flavours from around the world, including several from the Middle East, and each dish is as generous in size as it is in flavour. The thoughtfully curated wine list includes a strong natural selection and plenty of choice by the glass.

Name: Młoda Polska
Description En: Celebrity chef Beata Śniechowska's restaurant has a full name that translates as ‘Young Polish Bistro & Piano’, which feels like a pretty apt description. It’s run by a young and enthusiastic team, there's an invigorating bistro buzz to the atmosphere and there is indeed background music from the house pianist. The cooking dispenses with fuss and instead focuses on the natural flavours of quality ingredients, such as pure-white cod. A large vodka selection will please connoisseurs.

Name: Noriko Omakase
Description En: An engaging husband-and-wife team bring their natural charm to this intimate Japanese restaurant that relocated from Wrocław towards the end of 2022. The L-shaped counter seats just eight guests, who are encouraged to interact as the omakase menu unfolds. Largely imported produce is utilised in familiar dishes such as tuna temaki, chawanmushi and an array of nigiri. Japanese whiskies and a choice of sakes complete the memorable experience.

Name: Diuna
Description En: With a name meaning ‘sand dunes’, it’s no surprise to find this restaurant overlooking the dunes with the white sandy beach and Baltic Sea beyond. In summer, a table on the terrace is a must; if the weather keeps you inside, the views are better from the upstairs room. When you’re this close to the water, it makes sense to have seafood, so keep an eye out for some terrific skrei cod when in season. The meat options include beef Wellington to share when ordered in advance.

Name: Okovita
Description En: Run by the same team as Naama in the city centre, this suburban spot has a stylishly modern feel, while its voile curtains dividing the tables add an intimate air. The house-made sourdough gets the meal off to a great start, before the carefully conceived and skilfully executed dishes such as butterflied trout with braised cabbage and tomatoes. Add in the warm, friendly service and you have all the ingredients of a perfect neighbourhood haunt.

Name: Czosnek i Oliwa
Description En: On the outskirts of the Old Town, this vast restaurant offers a slick, buzzy dining experience in an industrial-style building arranged around a u-shaped courtyard. Diners are spread across two rooms: one with a bar and semi-open kitchen, the other large and airy with two mezzanines and floor-to-ceiling windows. The regularly changing menu is guided by the seasons and includes bright, generous dishes like beetroot carpaccio with goat’s cheese and pickled turnips.

Name: Masztalerz
Address: Arche Zamek Janów Podlaski Hotel, ul. Zamkowa 1, Janów Podlaski, 21-505, Poland
Description En: Located in the basement of the historic Zamek Janów Podlaski Hotel, which has its origins in the 15th century, there’s a suitably old-school, atmospheric feel to this vaulted, brick-lined restaurant. Choose dishes from across both the ‘Green’ (vegetarian and vegan) and ‘Red’ (meat and fish) menus which showcase the kitchen’s skill with classic techniques; Polish beef tenderloin comes with a rich demi-glace sauce, while the chocolate fondant for dessert is a classic version.

Name: Skórka Bistro Wino
Address: Hotel Villa Tradycja, ul. Włókiennicza 5, Białystok, 15-464, Poland
Description En: Located in the Villa Tradycja hotel, just outside the town centre, this bistro hosts guests across three distinct spaces: the front room with a grand piano played on Fridays and Saturdays; a more intimate dining room with blue panelling, red banquettes and shelves adorned with wine; and a terrace that’s ideal for sunny days. Throughout, the charming team serve nourishing dishes rooted in tradition, such as comforting chicken broth with dumplings.

Name: Murena
Description En: This modern sushi restaurant, decked out with yellow walls and dark furniture, occupies half of a larger space, with the other side being the colourful brunch and coffee spot, Seagull. The restaurant menu is all about spotlighting high-quality seafood, be that in the nigiri and sashimi with creative toppings and condiments, or the hot dishes that take on influences from around Asia, such as Korean-inspired aubergine with kimchi or a Malaysian laksa risotto.

Name: Oyster
Address: Radisson Blu Hotel, Aleja Baltic Park Molo 4, Świnoujście, 72-600, Poland
Description En: The name is an easy clue that this restaurant inside the Radisson Blu hotel is all about seafood. Although there are meat dishes, fish and shellfish lead the way on a menu where you could opt for a light, wallet-friendly meal or splash out and celebrate. Oysters are available to start, of course, but the Baltic herring is a great alternative and main dishes like halibut with spaghetti show subtle creativity while still highlighting the natural flavours of the ingredients.

Name: Boreczna
Description En: Hidden away among the Owl Mountains, you’ll find this rural oasis on a former farm. The eye-catching dining room has a slightly glitzy feel, with chandeliers and large candlelit tables. The cooking packs in plenty of flavour and shows off the kitchen’s technical skill with dishes like loin of veal with a meaty, multi-layered sauce. The service team are eager to please and, if you want to stay overnight, there are cosy bedrooms and even lodges in the grounds.

Name: Nafta Neo Bistro
Description En: Dining at this former coffin-making factory in an old industrial district feels like you’ve stumbled upon a secret little hideaway. The atmospheric bistro is spread across two rooms: the first has a red-brick, vintage feel with an open kitchen; the other is a winter garden room with a tree growing out of it and a bohemian atmosphere. In either, you’ll enjoy rustic, full-flavoured dishes with a hint of the Mediterranean. Friendly service helps maintain the relaxed atmosphere.

Name: Karakter
Description En: There's a lively atmosphere when eating at Karakter thanks to its loud music, cocktails and pared-back décor. The charming young team serve an extensive menu with a focus on offal, so be prepared for sweetbreads, brains and horse meat tartare, the last of which is one of their signature dishes. The cooking of these less-common ingredients is original and refined, blending many different flavours together. The set lunch menu is a steal.

Name: alewino
Description En: Spread across various rooms, this starkly decorated bistro started life as a wine shop. There’s still a range of bottles for sale, along with a wine list that offers plenty of younger and lesser-known producers. The menu allows guests to order a few plates to share, including staples like beef tartare along with dishes that show off seasonal vegetables, be that green asparagus or golden beetroot. Look out for the signpost by the gates when arriving, as the entrance is tucked away off the main street.

Name: Stary Dom
Description En: It might look unremarkable from outside, but there’s plenty of charm hiding within this large brasserie run like a well-oiled machine. Eye-catching beams and wooden mouldings add character to the high-ceilinged room, whose traditional vibe is matched by the food. The menu is resolutely classic, offering generous portions of big-flavoured dishes such as homemade pierogi or pork knuckle with honey-glazed crackling. A friendly team adds to the positive atmosphere.

Name: Złoty Groń
Address: Złoty Groń Resort & Spa, Istebna 593, Istebna, 43-470, Poland
Description En: Situated within the alpine resort of the same name, the views at this charmingly run restaurant are a serious draw. Whether seen from the terrace or the dining room, the sweeping countryside vistas are a treat. The cooking provides a worthy accompaniment to the setting with both an à la carte featuring aged Polish meats and a tasting menu showcasing the chef’s love of the region, via complex, occasionally nostalgic dishes based around prime local produce.

Name: GreenTable
Description En: With its light wooden furniture and on-view kitchen, there’s a pleasantly bright, open feel to this contemporary bistro. As the buzz of the chefs at work fills the room, choose from a selection of modernised Polish classics, whether that’s venison pierogi to start or miodownick honey cake to finish. There are a few Nordic touches to the cooking too (look out for skrei cod) and across the board the ingredients are seasoned well and adeptly cooked, so the unfussy preparations can really shine.

Name: Sublima
Address: Hotel New Skanpol, ul. Dworcowa 10, Kołobrzeg, 78-100, Poland
Description En: The smaller of two restaurants inside the Hotel New Skanpol in the centre of this Baltic Sea coastal town, Sublima is open throughout the day, with the offer stepping up a gear in the evening. Polish ingredients, classical French technique and subtle international flavours combine in dishes bursting with colour and flavour. The kitchen’s skill with fish cookery is particularly notable, as evidenced by terrific skrei cod with green asparagus, butter sauce and trout roe.

Name: Grand Kasprowy
Address: Bachleda Kasprowy Hotel, ul. Szymaszkowa 20, Zakopane, 34-500, Poland
Description En: Nestled within the Bachleda hotel, this well-run restaurant provides the perfect restoration after a tiring day skiing on the nearby slopes. Go for a table by the window if you can, so you can make the most of the views of the Tatra Mountains, then order from the comfortingly classic menu that specialises in prime cuts cooked over charcoal. From a range of steaks to local lamb, it’s hearty, satisfying fare. Don’t miss the apple pie with cinnamon ice cream to finish.

Name: Szyszka
Address: Hotel Seidorf, ul. Liczyrzepy 80, Sosnówka, 58-564, Poland
Description En: There has been a hotel on this site, perched on the Kazalnica hill, since 1899. Today called the Hotel Seidorf, it hosts this slightly formal restaurant with linen-laid tables and emblemed napkins. If there’s the opportunity to sit on the terrace, make sure you take it to absorb the stunning scenery. The cooking brings a refined touch to classic dishes, such as breaded pork loin with mashed potato, without losing their comforting feel and satisfying flavours.

Name: RAJ UTRACONY
Description En: There’s a proper neighbourhood feel to this Middle Eastern restaurant away from the city centre, where exposed ducting and concrete walls lend it an industrial-chic vibe. The dishes are designed for sharing and arrive all at once, featuring the likes of crispy green falafel or roasted lamb with charred chickpeas. To accompany the food, choose from a wine list specialising in natural options or from the range of house-made juices and mocktails.

Name: Meluzyna
Description En: With its classical mouldings, comfortable armchairs and attentive service, Meluzyna feels like a place you come to celebrate. Situated in the basement of a grand villa in a 19th-century neighbourhood, it counts a theatre and the Pomeranian Philharmonic as its neighbours. The cooking’s success is rooted in strong classical techniques and standout sauces, such as a deeply flavoured red wine sauce scented with rosemary, the ideal companion to slow-cooked beef cheeks.

Name: Epoka
Description En: Spread across two stylish, colourful rooms conceived by a Polish theatre designer – one bright blue, one in warmer hues – this restaurant inside the Raffles Europejski hotel takes its inspiration from historic Polish cookbooks. Classics like crayfish soup are listed on the menu next to their dates of origin, but given a modern spin in their execution. The largely local ingredients are presented to diners at the start of the meal and attentive, charming service completes the picture.

Name: Luneta & Lorneta Bistro Club
Description En: The Pałac Ciekocinko Hotel, a large house dating back to the 1920s, is home to this smart Belle Époque-style restaurant with a few plush details in its décor. Situated in the basement, there’s a pleasantly cosy feel to the dining room, which is accentuated by the cheery, welcoming service; a garden terrace is used to fine effect in the summer. The full-flavoured cooking incorporates French bistro and Italian influences such as confit duck leg and tarte Tatin.

Name: La Maddalena
Description En: Situated in a prime spot on the banks of the River Oder, there are few restaurants with a more enticing terrace than this. Ask for a seat here and, on a warm summer’s night, watch as darkness falls and the streetlights gleam on the river’s surface. The setting is matched by cooking that puts an emphasis on top-quality local meats – for dessert, look out for the chocolate fondant with a fruity punch. Let the knowledgeable staff guide you in picking complementary wines.

Name: ODRé
Description En: As you arrive at this deservedly busy spot by the Oder river, you quickly get the sense that you’re going to have a great time. The smiling, attentive team give you a warm welcome, before you head through the thick velvet curtains and discover the sleek, lively brasserie waiting within. From the bustling open kitchen, expect to see some French-based dishes such as a modern take on ‘escargots’ with garlic butter – all showcasing quality produce and executed with aplomb.

Name: arte
Address: Blow up Hall Hotel, ul. Kościuszki 42, Poznań, 61-891, Poland
Description En: The imposing former Stary Browar brewery was once filled with boiling hops and fermenting yeast, but today houses shops, an art gallery space and the sleekly modern Blow Up Hall hotel. Within the latter, arte lives up to its name with a creative streak running through dishes that take pride in Polish ingredients. Lunch is a lighter offering so come in the evening for the full experience, which culminates in imaginative desserts like their version of a crème brûlée.

Name: Lumière
Address: Hotel Edison, ul. Wypoczynkowa 60, Baranowo,, Przeźmierowo, 62-081, Poland
Description En: Sitting a stone’s throw from Lake Kierski and not far from Poznań airport, this restaurant within the Hotel Edison is something of a hidden gem. The cooking comes with a Polish heart and centres around colourful, imaginative dishes that fuse quality produce with a creative streak – such as cured trout from Zielenica with fennel, quail’s egg, buttermilk and dill. The hotel is surrounded by vines, meaning the wine list includes some none-more-local options.

Name: Polonaise
Address: Hilton Swinoujscie Resort & Spa, Aleja Baltic Park Molo 4, Świnoujście, 72-600, Poland
Description En: Named after the Polish national dance, this intimate restaurant is set within the Hilton Swinoujscie Resort & Spa. As you settle into the bright and colourful dining room, look out for the wines in illuminated cabinets and the meat and fish in ageing fridges. The menu mixes Polish aspects with a classical French base, in dishes such as lamb saddle with dauphinoise potato and mint pesto. The wine list features plenty of German options, with a few Polish ones too.

Name: Villa Greta
Description En: This collection of former farm buildings is named after the grandmother of the current generation of owners and incorporates a pottery workshop, shop, characterful bedrooms and this homely bistro. The vaulted red-brick ceiling and wood-burning stove give it a rustic feel, while the lovely garden and terrace allow you to soak up the rural peace and quiet. The cooking offers hearty classics such as a full-flavoured bigos with deer and rye bread.

Name: Carska
Description En: With a name meaning ‘tsar’, this uniquely positioned restaurant sits inside a hotel occupying what was once the Tsar’s private railway station, used to reach his vast shooting estate. The surrounding forestry is now a UNESCO World Heritage site and is home to a large population of European bison. Dine in the former railway hall or, in summer, an old train carriage, and enjoy cooking with a traditional heart, such as fried deer tenderloin with a seasonally changing garnish.

Name: Między Mostami
Description En: Modern interpretations of Polish classics are a feature at this stylishly designed brasserie. Tartare, beef tongue and blood sausage are the kind of dishes you can expect, delivered with a refined and delicate touch. For dessert, look out for a nuts and cookies concoction inspired by the chef’s grandmother. Cocktails are a feature too, with a large bar, extensive list and able mixologist on hand. A tasting menu restaurant from the same team, Most, is located to the rear.

Name: Sztuczka
Description En: Situated opposite the striking architecture of the Museum of the Second World War, this restaurant boasts elegant contemporary design, where brightly coloured banquettes and velour chairs blend with globe pendant lights and a parquet floor. The dishes – built on French classics like beef tartare and turbot with beurre blanc – are detailed, well-composed and blissfully free of superfluous elements. The friendly service team show palpable pride in their work.

Name: Gustaw
Address: ul. Księdza Piotra Skargi 18A, Wrocław, 50-082, Poland
Description En: With its bright décor, marble-topped tables and unusual sunken dining area, this must be one of the most strikingly designed restaurants in the city – and that’s without mentioning its fascinating location within what remains of the old Bastion Sakwowy fortification. The cooking is similarly eye-catching, with classically based dishes coming with vibrant colours and a stylish touch. The elegant, slightly formal atmosphere matches the surroundings.

Name: The Time
Description En: This smart monochrome restaurant sits within a refurbished city centre mansion, which also houses its sister restaurants and an office space; it's somewhat hidden away within the complex, but well worth seeking out. Formerly a grill-centric eatery, the Mibrasa charcoal oven remains in use for produce like tomahawk steak, but these days the menu is more expansive and could include their standout marinated herring, which delivers all the expected zing and vibrancy. There are some seriously good wines on offer too.

Name: Scoria
Description En: ‘Scoria’ refers to a type of volcanic rock, one which inspires some of the interior design at this chic modern restaurant on the banks of the Brda river. A window into the kitchen allows you to watch the chefs as they craft classic European dishes such as lobster tail with saffron risotto, alongside more Polish creations like duck leg with potato dumplings. Many of the dishes can be made extra luxurious by adding black truffle or Antonius caviar.

Name: Hankki
Description En: Located in the up-and-coming Zabłocie neighbourhood, this sister restaurant to Hana Sushi is located on the ground floor of a modern apartment block. Inside, it’s bright and stylish, with an abundance of blonde wood furnishings. Despite bento boxes for lunch and a selection of nigiri, there’s more of a Korean slant to the menu here, with hearty, soul-warming options like red jjamppong. Don’t miss the signature popcorn chicken too!

Name: Babinicz
Address: Resort Dworzysko, aleja Spacerowa 22, Szczawno-Zdrój, 58-310, Poland
Description En: As you enter this restaurant at the heart of the sprawling Dworzysko estate, it very quickly sets out its stall. A fridge filled with prime meats, along with animal heads lining the walls, add to the feel of an old-school hunting lodge, and indeed Polish meats are at the core of the menu. Steaks of various shapes and sizes are a feature, aged in-house and delivering plenty of flavour. The delightful team are genuinely eager to please and do their bit to enhance the experience.

Name: Ogień i Sól
Description En: Set in the striking regenerated Geyer Gardens district, this former factory has retained an on-trend industrial edge to its interiors, with the exposed red-brick walls and open kitchen catching the eye. Steaks are at the heart of the menu, cooked over charcoal either on or off the bone and served with a choice of sauces. The quality of the dry-aged meat provides plenty of flavour, with some wagyu options available if you’re looking to celebrate in style.

Name: Marino Bistrot
Description En: Hidden away in a residential area, this basement restaurant sports rustic exposed brickwork and simple bistro furnishings. It’s named after Chef-Owner Livio Marino, who has a passion for authentic Italian dishes that manifests itself here in an extensive menu that includes a selection of homemade pastas. Look out for the pasta dishes and the likes of sea bream cooked over an open fire. For dessert, it’s very hard to resist tiramisu in a place like this.

Name: Mercado Nuevo
Description En: This younger sister to Mercado Tapas Bistro sits underneath the next railway arch and is a smaller, more intimate space, boasting closely set tables and the chatter of diners blending into the rumble of trains overhead. Like its sibling, the menu has a Spanish heart but this time mixes in more globally minded small plates, such as pork ribs with miso glaze or the standout ricotta agnolotti. Spanish wines are to the fore and the service team run things smoothly.

Name: Yes Butcher! Shop & Bistro
Address: Stare Koszary, ul. Wojskowa 4, Poznań, 60-792, Poland
Description En: Steaks, steaks and more steaks are the order of the day at this butcher’s shop and restaurant housed in part of the reinvented former army barracks at Stare Koszary. Thankfully, those steaks are of great quality and are cooked with an assured hand. Beef from the US, Argentina and Australia are on offer, but it’s worth going for the Polish Hereford Heifer for its flavour and value for money. Non-steak dishes include burgers, merguez sausages and fish of the day.
